Hi, quick query

for the above image
1) why a black box is coming? are emojis not supported?
2) How do you get the red output automatically below #eval? In TPIL, other places also show the output of #check or #eval in blue line below it, how to enable this?

3) How do you get the eye, to hide certain things?
4) is copy button autosupported by verso? or custom JS is to be added?

The answer to 2 is that this is actually a documentation warning: It is supposed to display the output, but the message in the documentation does not match the message it gives when the document is compiled. Notice that the text that is below is not the actual output of eval, it describes both the actual and expected output.
From wherever i noticed, both had same answers. Still how do you enable it??
Ah, apologies, I was wrong, indeed. I don't understand the what's really going on here, so let's wait for someone who actually knows:)

Anirudh Gupta said:

2) How do you get the red output automatically below #eval? In TPIL, other places also show the output of #check or #eval in blue line below it, how to enable this?

3) How do you get the eye, to hide certain things?
4) is copy button autosupported by verso? or custom JS is to be added?

All of these are part of the custom setup for TPiL. The book was ported from a custom Markdown-based setup that featured the hide/show buttons so that every example was completely self-contained, and the Verso setup preserves that property. It also uses comments for some purposes that more idiomatic Verso would use a custom code block for.

That said - a copy button and showing output inline are generally useful, and should be upstreamed to Verso itself.

I'll look into the black box.
i see. Thanks! ill look into these.

One more question

Just like the heading page has "CONTENTS" header on this page

say htmlDepth := 3 is set for me, so a subheader will also have now a page which will enlist its content pages, but that page does not have "CONTENTS" header. How do I add one to that page??

Setting this metadata should do the trick for pages that themselves have sub-pages:

# My header
%%%
htmlToc := true
%%%

The contents of the current page are in the left side.
@David Thrane Christiansen thanks, if i want to change the name of Contents to something else, is it possible?

I don't believe so.

What's your use case?

David Thrane Christiansen said:

I don't believe so.

What's your use case?

for the cookbook i was making, i wanted to put "Recipes" as header.
Ah, that makes sense! I'd accept a PR that allowed this to be overridden
do u know which file to edit or which CSS to change? ill try something

The thing to do would be to add it to Manual.PartMetadata as a String field that defaults to "Contents", then find the place in VersoManual.lean where the header is constructed and replace the hard-coded "Contents" with the value of that field.

Hi i was trying out verso-blog example, and i saw this in advanced blogs example from verso-templates

Why does on hover this comes? and sometimes when i hover over Expr it shows Nat's definition, which is a bit weird.

This is probably a bad caching setup on the web server.

To avoid having a copy of Nat's docstring for every occurrence of Nat in a document, Verso extracts all the hovers to a deduplicated JSON file. Each of them gets an ID during rendering. If the JSON file and the IDs are out of sync, then some may be missing and some may point at the wrong hover info.

Sometimes the Python web server caches things that it shouldn't, and doesn't notice that a file has changed on disk. Try restarting the web server and see if it goes away. If so, I'll look at setting the Python server to not cache JSON files.
Oh yes, i rebuilt and emptied cache, it is working great! Thanks!
